body:
This might be the same issue that I get when setting `enableIvy: true` in my project, but I find the description here pretty vague.

`tsconfig.json`:
```
{
  "compilerOptions": {
     // ...
    "paths": {"config": ["src/config.dev.ts"]}
  },
  "angularCompilerOptions": { "enableIvy": true }
}
```

When building, this with Angular 8.1.0, I'm getting an`ERROR in ENOTDIR: not a directory, scandir '{...}/client/src/config.dev.ts'`, which makes me think there's an assumption that the path mappings always map to a directory. Setting an exception breakpoint allowed me to get the stack trace:
```
Error
    at handleErrorFromBinding (fs.js:126:5)
    at Object.readdirSync (fs.js:795:3)
    at NodeJSFileSystem.readdir (node_modules/@angular/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/file_system/src/node_js_file_system.js:37:74)
    at EntryPointFinder.walkDirectoryForEntryPoints (node_modules/@angular/compiler-cli/ngcc/src/packages/entry_point_finder.js:85:18)
    at node_modules/@angular/compiler-cli/ngcc/src/packages/entry_point_finder.js:36:123
    at Array.reduce (<anonymous>)
    at EntryPointFinder.findEntryPoints (node_modules/@angular/compiler-cli/ngcc/src/packages/entry_point_finder.js:36:49)
    at Object.mainNgcc [as process] (node_modules/@angular/compiler-cli/ngcc/src/main.js:68:25)
    at NgccProcessor.processModule (node_modules/@ngtools/webpack/src/ngcc_processor.js:54:16)
    at node_modules/@ngtools/webpack/src/compiler_host.js:317:36
```

Maybe the `EntryPointFinder` should check if the path mappings do in fact map to a directory or not.

body: I think you are right, @michael42. The changes in #30525 affect how pathMappings are used, but doesn't solve the problem in its current state (see https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/30525/files#r300829346).
Getting same issue, for me it's the environment files that give IVY a headache..
This should be fixed as part of https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/30525

ERROR in ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat 'E:/Users/Juliano/Documents/Projetos/SA-R/sar-frontend/node_modules/linqts/index.ts'
In fact, there's no `index.ts` on the folder mentioned on the error message. Is it a problem that I should post on `linqts` repo?

Well, the compiler didn't like the `undefined` value: 

ERROR in The "path" argument must be of type string. Received type object
Is there a way to force it to accept it? [UPDATE]: it accepted `'dist/index.js'` instead of `undefined`
Interesting that it failed with the `undefined`... glad you got a workaround working.

```
yarn ivy-ngcc -l debug -t linqts
```

leads to

This will be fixed by https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/31509

Good to know! After following you fixing that one, I found a dependency (`ng2-file-upload`), that became the next issue during compilation. It's maintained by valor-software. I'm reporting it to you here because it's kind of old (it uses @angular@2.x.x). Honestly, it seems to be abandoned (for this Ivy testing I've just replaced it by an updated version made available by another user of that library). My question is: should I report to you guys this kind of thing (very old angular-based dependencies) or save your time and just replace it in these projects (it's not healthy to keep abandoned projects as dependencies anyway).
